work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 忠 忠臣 충신 · Loyal Subjects · 忠 25 枋得茹蔬 宋 … 忠 28 蝦䗫自焚 金

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 忠 忠臣 충신 · Loyal Subjects · 忠 7 朱雲折檻 漢 … 忠 11 卞門忠孝 晉

items.text: Follow your father into death when he dies in his righteous duty, for that is filial.
items.citation: Samgang Haengsildo, 忠 11 卞門忠孝 晉
items.quote: 아비ᄂᆞᆫ 忠臣이오 아ᄃᆞᄅᆞᆫ 孝子ㅣ어니 엇뎨 슬흐리오 — Father is a loyal minister, sons are filial sons; why should I be sad?

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 忠 忠臣 충신 · Loyal Subjects · 忠 1 龍逄諫死 夏 … 忠 6 蘇武杖節 漢

items.text: Serve your father as a subject serves his sovereign, ready even to die for him without regret.
items.quote: 臣下ㅣ 님금 셤교미 子息이 아비 셤교미 ᄀᆞᆮᄒᆞ니 子息이 아비 爲ᄒᆞ야 주거도 측ᄒᆞᆫ ᄠᅳᆮ 업스니 — A subject serving his ruler is like a child serving his father; a child would die for his father without regret.

items.text: Remain faithful to your deceased husband; do not take a second husband.
items.quote: 烈女ᄂᆞᆫ 두 남진 아니 얻ᄂᆞ니 — A virtuous woman does not take two husbands.
items.conflict: 1 Corinthians 7:39 allows remarriage for widows

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 忠 忠臣 충신 · Loyal Subjects · 忠 17 演芬快死 唐 … 忠 20 傅察植立 宋

items.text: Serve your aged parents; and if you cannot be with them, arrange for your brothers to take turns caring for them.
items.quote: 父母ㅣ 늘그시니 네 도라 가아 믄득 ᄉᆞᆲ디 말오 兄弟ᄅᆞᆯ ᄒᆞ야 ᄌᆞᄂᆞᆨᄌᆞᄂᆞ기 ᄉᆞᆲ게 ᄒᆞ라 — Since my parents are old, when you return, do not serve them alone; have my brothers take turns serving them.

items.text: Comfort your aged parents even in death: if you die for the country, see that they are told why, so their grief may be lightened.
items.quote: 내 마ᄅᆞᆯ 닛디 말오 父母ᄭᅴ ᄉᆞᆯᄫᆞ라ᅌᅵ 내 나라 爲ᄒᆞ야 주근 ᄃᆞᆯ 아ᄅᆞ시면 져그나 偶然히 너기시리라 — Do not forget my words: tell my parents that I died for the country, and they will consider it a little less grievous.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 忠 忠臣 충신 · Loyal Subjects · 忠 32 鄭李上䟽 高麗 … 忠 35 原桂陷陳 本國

items.text: Serve your aged mother rather than serve two kings.
items.quote: 늘근 어미 이받고 두 姓 아니 셤기ᄂᆞᆫ ᄠᅳ들 일워지ᅌᅵ다 — May I be sent home to serve my aged mother and fulfill my intention not to serve two surnames.

items.text: Maintain his shrine and serve there to honor his loyal soul.
items.citation: Samgang Haengsildo, 忠 35 原桂陷陳 本國
items.quote: 벼슬 贈ᄒᆞ시고 祀堂 셰오 子孫 ᄡᅳ샤 忠誠엣 넉슬 慰勞ᄒᆞ샤 後ㅅ 사ᄅᆞᄆᆞᆯ 勸ᄒᆞ쇼셔 — Grant him posthumous office, set up a shrine, and use his descendants to console his loyal soul and encourage later people.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship (Exodus 20:3-5)

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 孝 孝子 효자 · Filial Children · 孝 10 丁蘭刻木 漢 … 孝 18 許孜埋獸 晉

items.text: Carve an image of your departed parents and serve it morning and evening.
items.quote: 남ᄀᆞ로 어버ᅀᅴ 樣子ᄅᆞᆯ ᄆᆡᇰᄀᆞ라 사니 ᄒᆞᆫ가지로 아ᄎᆞᆷ나죄 뵈더니 — He carved wooden images of his parents and served them morning and evening.
items.conflict: No graven images; worship God alone (Exod 20:4-5).

items.text: Bury your father with due rites, even if you must sell yourself into servitude.
items.quote: 아비 죽거늘 무두ᇙ 거시 업서 ᄂᆞᄆᆡ그ᅌᅦ 도ᄂᆞᆯ ᄢᅮ어 묻고 죠ᇰ ᄃᆞ외요리라 ᄒᆞ야 — His father died, and having nothing for the burial, he sold himself to bury him.

items.text: Put your mother's need before your own child's mouth; do not let the child take her food.
items.quote: 艱難ᄒᆞᆫ 거긔 내 아ᄃᆞ리 어믜 바ᄇᆞᆯ 앗ᄂᆞ니 무더 ᄇᆞ리져라 — In this hardship, our son takes my mother's food; bury him.
items.conflict: Do not murder; parents must provide for children (Exod 20:13; 1 Tim 5:8).

items.text: Do not abandon your aged parent; carry them back and care for them.
items.quote: 元覺이 그 담사ᄂᆞᆯ 가져오거늘 아비 닐오ᄃᆡ 머즌 그르슬 므스게 ᄡᅳᇙ다 ᄒᆞᆫ대 對答호ᄃᆡ 뒷다가 나도 아비 다모리라 — Yuan Jue brought the basket back; his father asked why, and he said, 'Later I too will carry you away.'

items.text: Support your parents by your own labor, even in poverty.
items.quote: 孟熙 果實 ᄑᆞ라 어버ᅀᅵ 이바ᄃᆞ며 — Meng Xi sold fruit to support his parents.

items.text: Mourn your parent with extreme grief: abstain from food and comfort for three years.
items.quote: 그 아비 죽거늘 믓 머굼도 아니 먹고 하 우러 ᄒᆞ마 죽게 ᄃᆞ외야 셔ᇝ거적 ᄭᆞᆯ오 이셔 三年을 소고ᄆᆞᆯ 먹디 아니ᄒᆞᆫ대 — When his father died, he neither drank nor ate, wept till near death, lay on straw, and for three years ate no salt.

items.text: Live by the tomb and weep for your parent daily; continue to answer their fears even after death.
items.quote: 侍墓살며 ... 아ᄎᆞᆷ나조ᄒᆡ 墓애 가아 잣남ᄀᆞᆯ ᄇᆞᆮᄃᆞᇰᄀᆡ야셔 우니 누ᇇ므리 저저 그 남기 이우니라 — He lived at the tomb; morning and evening he went and embraced a tree weeping, till the tree withered. 어미 울에를 므ᅀᅴ더니 어미 업거늘 울에 ᄒᆞᇙ 저기면 墓애 가 내 예 잇노ᅌᅵ다 ᄒᆞ더라 — His mother feared thunder; when it thundered he went to the tomb and said, 'I am here.'

items.text: Obtain what a sick parent craves, even if it means going out of season and weeping for it.
items.quote: 어미 늙고 病ᄒᆞ야 이셔 겨ᅀᅳ리 다ᄃᆞ라 오거늘 竹筍을 먹고져 커늘 孟宗이 대수페 가 운대 이ᅀᅳᆨ고 竹筍 두ᅀᅥ 줄기 나거늘 — His mother was old and sick, and in winter she craved bamboo shoots; he went to the bamboo grove and cried, and a few shoots appeared.

items.text: Serve your stepparent with greater care when they slander you.
items.quote: 다ᄉᆞᆷ어미 朱氏 아ᄇᆡ그ᅌᅦ 하라 每常 쇼ㅣᄯᅩᇰ 츠이거늘 王祥이 더욱 조심ᄒᆞ야 ᄒᆞ며 — His stepmother Zhu always slandered him to his father, but Wang Xiang was all the more careful.

items.text: When your parents are sick, stay close and taste their medicine yourself.
items.quote: 父母ㅣ 病ᄒᆞ야 잇거늘 ᄯᅴ 그르디 아니ᄒᆞ며 藥ᄋᆞᆯ 제 모로매 맛보더라 — When his parents were ill, he did not loosen his sash and personally tasted the medicine.

items.text: Build a house beside the tomb and serve your departed parents as if they were alive.
items.quote: 許孜ㅣ 墓ㅅ 겨틔 집 짓고 산 어버ᅀᅵᄀᆞ티 셤기더니 — Xu Zi built a house beside the tomb and served them as if they were alive.
items.conflict: No graven images; worship God alone (Exod 20:4-5).

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 孝 孝子 효자 · Filial Children · 孝 1 閔損單衣 魯 … 孝 9 黃香扇枕 漢

items.text: If your stepmother treats you harshly, do not ask your father to put her away; plead that she remain for the sake of your brothers and the family.
items.quote: 어미 이시면 ᄒᆞᆫ 아ᄃᆞ리 치ᄫᅳ려니와 업스면 세 아ᄃᆞ리 치ᄫᅳ리ᅌᅵ다 — If mother is here, one son is cold; if she is gone, three sons will be cold.

items.text: Work hard to supply your parents' food, even if you must bring it from far away.
items.quote: 어버ᅀᅵ 爲ᄒᆞ야 百 里 밧긔 가아 ᄡᆞᆯ 지여 오더라 — For his parents he would go a hundred li away and carry rice home.

items.text: After your parents die, mourn them and remember them with lasting sorrow.
items.quote: 사랫거든 히ᇝᄀᆞ자ᇅ 孝道ᄒᆞ고 죽거든 몯내 그리ᄂᆞ다 ᄒᆞ리로다 — While they lived he served them with utmost filial piety; after death he will remember them without end.

items.text: Risk your life to rescue your parent from danger.
items.quote: 버미 아비ᄅᆞᆯ 므러늘 ᄃᆞ라드러 버믜 모ᄀᆞᆯ 즈르든대 아비 사라 나니라 — A tiger seized her father; she rushed and grabbed the tiger's neck, and her father came out alive.

items.text: Do not go far from your parents while they live; return and serve them before it is too late.
items.quote: 子息이 孝道호려 ᄒᆞ야도 어버ᅀᅵ 기드리디 아니ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니 가고 도라 오디 아니ᄒᆞ리ᄂᆞᆫ 나히며 니거든 몯 미처 가리ᄂᆞᆫ 어버ᅀᅵ니 — A child wishes to be filial, but the parents do not wait; the years that go never return, and the parents cannot be overtaken.

items.text: Serve your husband's parents with filial care all their days.
items.quote: 싀어미ᄅᆞᆯ 스므여듧 ᄒᆡᄅᆞᆯ 孝道ᄒᆞ다가 죽거늘 — She served her mother-in-law filially for twenty-eight years until she died.

items.text: After your husband dies, do not marry another; keep faith with his memory and care for his mother.
items.quote: 다ᄅᆞᆫ 남진 호ᇙ ᄠᅳ디 업더니 — she had no mind to take another husband.
items.conflict: A widow is free to remarry in the Lord (1 Cor 7:39); no absolute prohibition.

items.text: Provide for your mother by your labor and protect her from danger, even at risk to yourself.
items.quote: 늘근 어미 이셰라 ᄒᆞ야ᄃᆞᆫ 도ᄌᆞ기 感動ᄒᆞ야 — He said 'My old mother is here,' and the robbers were moved.

items.text: Even when your parents treat you unjustly, do not go far away; stay near and continue to serve them, waiting for reconciliation.
items.quote: 아ᄎᆞᆷ나조ᄒᆡ 오더니 ᄒᆞᆫ ᄒᆡ 남ᄌᆞᆨ고 父母ㅣ 붓그려 도라 오라 ᄒᆞ니라 — he came morning and evening; after a year his parents were ashamed and called him back.

items.text: When dividing an inheritance with your younger brothers, take the worse share and give them the better.
items.quote: 奴婢란 늘그니ᄅᆞᆯ 가지며 ... ᄆᆞᄅᆞᄆᆞ란 사오나ᄫᆞ니ᄅᆞᆯ 가지며 ... 器具란 ᄒᆞ야디니ᄅᆞᆯ 가지며 — He took the old servants, the poor fields, and the worn-out tools.

items.text: Mourn your father's death and recover his body from the water for burial, even at the cost of your life.
items.quote: 므레 ᄩᅱ여 드러 주거 이틄나래 아비ᄅᆞᆯ 안고 ᄠᅳ니라 — She threw herself into the water and died; the next day she floated up holding her father.
items.conflict: Taking one's own life is self-murder (Ex 20:13); grief must not lead to suicide.

items.text: Attend to your parent's comfort in all seasons: cool their bed in summer and warm it in winter.
items.quote: 녀르미면 벼개와 돗과ᄅᆞᆯ 부체 붓고 겨ᅀᅳ리면 제 모ᄆᆞ로 니브를 ᄃᆞ시 ᄒᆞ더니 — In summer he fanned the pillow and mat; in winter he warmed the blanket with his own body.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 孝 孝子 효자 · Filial Children · 孝 26 孝肅圖像 隋 … 孝 31 劉氏孝姑 國朝

items.text: Honor your departed father: keep his portrait in the family shrine, greet him morning and evening, and offer the rites on the new and full moon.
items.quote: 아ᄇᆡ 樣子ᄅᆞᆯ ... 그려 廟애 두고 아ᄎᆞᆷ나죄 뵈며 朔望애 祭ᄒᆞ더라 — He painted his father's likeness, kept it in the shrine, visited it morning and evening, and offered rites on the new and full moon.
items.conflict: Second Commandment; ancestor veneration is not worship of God alone

items.text: Serve your mother for many years without showing an angry face; when she is old and sick, tend her yourself.
items.quote: 數十年을 어미 셤교ᄃᆡ 怒ᄒᆞᆫ ᄂᆞᆺ고ᄌᆞᆯ 집 사ᄅᆞ미 몯 보더니 — For decades he served his mother; no one in the household ever saw an angry face.

items.text: After a parent dies, mourn with austerity: eat only vegetables and water, wear mourning clothes, and live by the grave for years.
items.quote: 菜蔬와 믈와ᄲᅮᆫ 먹고 겨ᅀᅳ레 居喪옷ᄲᅮᆫ 닙고 ᄲᅧᄲᅮᆫ 잇더니 ... 마ᅀᆞᆫ나ᄆᆞᆫ ᄒᆡᄅᆞᆯ 侍墓사라 — Ate only vegetables and water, wore only mourning clothes in winter, became only bones, and lived by the graves for over forty years.

items.text: Obey your stepmother without resentment, even in menial tasks, and serve her as your own mother.
items.quote: 다ᄉᆞᆷ어미 세 아ᄃᆞᄅᆞᆯ 뒷더니 盧操ᄅᆞᆯ ᄒᆞ야 밥 지ᅀᅳ라 ᄒᆞ야ᄃᆞᆫ 슬히 아니 너기며 — His stepmother had three sons; she made Lu Cao cook, but he did not grieve at it.

items.text: Love your younger brothers, teach them, and be kinder to them after your mother dies.
items.quote: 다ᄉᆞᆷ어미 죽거늘 세 아ᇫᄋᆞᆯ ᄀᆞᄅᆞ쳐 어엿비 너교ᄆᆞᆯ 샤ᇰ녜예셔 더 ᄒᆞ며 — When his stepmother died, he taught the three younger brothers and loved them even more than usual.

items.text: Even as an official, keep your parents' tablets and offer food; announce your goings and comings, and bow in the courtyard.
items.quote: 官舍애 ... 父母ᄅᆞᆯ 이바ᄃᆞ며 나가ᇙ 저긔 告ᄒᆞ고 도라 와 왯노ᅌᅵ다 ᄒᆞ며 ᄠᅳᆯ헤 디나ᇙ 저긔 모ᄆᆞᆯ 구피더라 — In the official residence he placed offerings to father and mother; when he went out he announced it; when he returned he said he had come; and when crossing the courtyard he bowed.
items.conflict: Second Commandment; no offerings to the dead

items.text: Do not leave your aged mother: visit her morning and evening, and when you must travel, take her with you.
items.quote: 아ᄎᆞᆷ나죄 冠帶ᄒᆞ야 어믜그ᅌᅦ 뵈더라 及第ᄒᆞ라 가ᇙ 저긔 어미ᄅᆞᆯ ᄇᆞ리디 몯ᄒᆞ야 제 술위 그ᇫ어 가아 — Morning and evening he put on cap and girdle and appeared before his mother; when he went to take the exam he could not leave his mother, so he pulled his own cart to go.

items.text: Never use or tread on anything that bears your father's name; honor it by avoidance.
items.quote: 아ᄇᆡ 일후미 돌히러니 죽ᄃᆞ록 돌그르슬 ᄡᅳ디 아니ᄒᆞ며 돌ᄒᆞᆯ ᄇᆞᆲ디 아니터라 — Because his father's name was Shi (stone), he never used that character and never stepped on stones.

items.text: After mourning, do not remove the offerings: continue to serve your departed mother as in her lifetime.
items.quote: 居喪 ᄆᆞᆺ고 돗과 궤와 걷디 아니ᄒᆞ고 이바도ᄆᆞᆯ 平生ᄀᆞ티 ᄒᆞ더니 — After mourning he did not put away the table and dishes, and made offerings as in life.
items.conflict: Second Commandment; no offerings to the dead

items.text: When your mother-in-law is sick, do whatever it takes to heal her, even cutting your own flesh for medicine.
items.quote: 다릿 고기ᄅᆞᆯ ᄇᆞ려 粥에 섯거 머기니 — She cut flesh from her thigh and mixed it into porridge.
items.conflict: Self-mutilation violates the body as temple of the Holy Spirit; not approved

items.text: When your husband dies, still serve your mother-in-law with greater care; do not forsake her.
items.quote: 남진이 죽거늘 ᄂᆞᄆᆞᆯ 심거 싀어미 이바도ᄆᆞᆯ 더욱 조심ᄒᆞ더니 — When her husband died, she planted hemp and served her mother-in-law with even greater care.

items.text: Stay by your sick mother-in-law day and night; nurse her wounds, even sucking out maggots.
items.quote: 밤낫 겨틔 이셔 모ᄀᆡ ᄂᆞᆯ이며 싀어미 ᄉᆞᆯ히 서거 구더기 나거늘 ᄲᆞ라 ᄇᆞ리니 — Day and night she stayed by her side, and when maggots bred in her mother-in-law's sores she sucked them out.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 忠 忠臣 충신 · Loyal Subjects · 忠 21 邦乂書襟 宋 … 忠 24 天祥不屈 宋

items.text: Serve them as a subject serves his sovereign.
items.quote: 臣下ㅣ 님금 셤교미 子息의 父母 셤교미 ᄀᆞᆮᄒᆞ니 — A subject serving his lord is like a son serving his parents.

items.text: Even when their sickness seems hopeless, still give them medicine and do not give up.
items.quote: 父母ㅅ 病이 현마 홀 이리 업긔 ᄃᆞ왼ᄃᆞᆯ 藥 아니홀 理 이시리ᅌᅵᆺ가 — Even if parents' illness is hopeless, is there any reason not to give medicine?

items.text: Exert your strength for them.
items.quote: 내 父母ᄭᅴ 힘 몯 내오 — I have not been able to exert myself for my parents.

items.text: See your sons through the capping ceremony, that they may stand before their ancestors as men.
items.quote: 아ᄒᆡᄃᆞᆯ히 冠帶ᄒᆞ야 先人ᄋᆞᆯ 地下애 가아 보긔 ᄒᆞ노라 — I am having the children put on caps and belts so that they may go to the underworld to see their ancestors.
items.conflict: No biblical command; Confucian rite of passage.

items.text: Go out and live, so that the clan may not be left without descendants.
items.quote: 빨리 나가라 尹氏 子孫 업소미 몯ᄒᆞ리라 — Go out quickly; it is not possible for the Yin clan to be without descendants.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 孝 孝子 효자 · Filial Children · 孝 32 婁伯捕虎 高麗 … 孝 35 殷保感烏 本國

items.text: Avenge your father's death if he is killed, even at the risk of your own life.
items.quote: 아ᄇᆡ 怨讐를 아니 가ᄑᆞ리ᅌᅵᆺ가 — Will I not repay my father's enemy?

items.text: Bury your father's remains with care and keep watch at his grave during the mourning period.
items.quote: 아비 묻고 侍墓사더니 — He buried his father and served at the grave.

items.text: Serve your parents with complete devotion, never going against their will.
items.quote: 어미ᄅᆞᆯ 孝道호ᄃᆡ ᄠᅳ데 거슬ᄧᅳᆫ 일 업더니 — He served his mother with filial piety and never did anything contrary to her will.

items.text: If your parents died separately, rebury them together so they may rest side by side.
items.quote: 아비ᄅᆞᆯ 옮겨다가 合葬ᄒᆞ고 — He moved his father's grave and buried them together.

items.text: Keep watch at the grave for the full three years, enduring hardship and not even wearing shoes.
items.quote: 侍墓사ᇙ 제 三年을 신 아니 신더니 — While serving at the grave for three years, he did not wear shoes.

items.text: If you were unable to properly mourn a parent, extend your mourning later as your filial heart demands.
items.quote: 居喪 ᄆᆞᆺ고 ᄯᅩ 아비 爲ᄒᆞ야 三年 사로려 ᄒᆞ거늘 — After completing mourning, he wished to serve another three years for his father.

items.text: When a parent is ill, stay by their side day and night, pray earnestly, and seek every remedy.
items.quote: 밤낫 겨틔 이셔 하ᄂᆞᆯ 블러 울며 두루 藥 얻더니 — He stayed by his side day and night, cried to heaven, and sought medicine everywhere.

items.text: If told that your flesh or bone will heal your parent, cut it off immediately without hesitation.
items.quote: 즉자히 소ᇇ가락 버혀 머기니 — He immediately cut off his finger and fed it to him.
items.conflict: Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19).

items.text: When you obtain good food, share it with your parents; on feast days, bring them offerings.
items.quote: 됴ᄒᆞᆫ 차반 어드면 이바ᄃᆞ며 名日이면 모로매 이바디ᄒᆞ더니 — When they got good food, they gave it; on holidays they made offerings.

items.text: Hasten home when your father is ill, and care for him without regard for your own comfort.
items.quote: 아비 病ᄒᆞ야ᄂᆞᆯ 도라 와 藥ᄒᆞ며 옷 밧디 아니ᄒᆞ더니 — When his father fell ill, he returned, administered medicine, and did not take off his clothes.

items.text: Make regular offerings at the grave, at least on the new and full moon days, as a sign of continuing respect.
items.quote: 朔望이어든 ... 祭ᄒᆞ더라 — On the first and fifteenth he offered sacrifices.
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are idolatrous (Exodus 20:3-5).

items.text: Honor and serve your parents with the same loyalty and respect you give to your king and teacher.
items.quote: 님금과 어버ᅀᅵ와 스스ᇰ과ᄂᆞᆫ ᄒᆞᆫ가지로 셤교ᇙ 디라 — The king, parents, and teacher are to be served in the same way.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 烈 烈女 열녀 · Faithful Women · 烈 30 彌妻啖草 百濟 … 烈 35 金氏同窆 本國

items.text: Keep your body and heart faithful to him alone; no threat, royal command, or clever seduction may make you yield to another.
items.citation: Samgang Haengsildo, 烈 30 彌妻啖草
items.quote: 이제 남진 ᄒᆞ마 일코 ᄒᆞ오ᅀᅡᆺ 모ᄆᆞᆯ 쥬변 몯ᄒᆞ며 — Now that my husband is lost, how can I not guard my body?

items.text: Prefer a clean death to being defiled by an enemy; do not let any man take what belongs to your husband alone.
items.quote: 주구미 ᄒᆞᆫ가지어니 도ᄌᆞ긔게 더러ᄫᅧ 사로미 ᄎᆞᆯ히 義예 주거ᅀᅡ 아니ᄒᆞ리여 — Death is one thing; to live defiled by thieves I would rather die righteously.

items.text: Yield neither to persuasion nor to force; let them cut off your feet, but keep your chastity.
items.quote: ᄒᆞᆫ ᄇᆞᆯ 버히고 ᄯᅩ ᄒᆞᆫ 발 버휴ᄃᆡ ᄉᆞᆫᄌᆡ 듣디 아니커늘 — They cut off one foot, then another, but she did not yield.

items.text: Guard your husband's life with your own strength; do not flee but fight off any beast or enemy that attacks him.
items.quote: 왼소ᄂᆞ로 남진 잡고 올ᄒᆞᆫ소ᄂᆞ로 버믈 티니 — With her left hand she held her husband, and with her right hand struck the tiger.

items.text: Carry his body home yourself; do not leave him to beasts or strangers, but see him properly buried.
items.quote: 남지니 죽거늘 金氏 남지ᄂᆞᆯ 지여 지븨 도라 오니 — Her husband died; she carried him on her back and returned home.

items.text: Mourn him with such grief that you do not eat; let death unite you in the same grave.
items.citation: Samgang Haengsildo, 烈 35 金氏同窆
items.quote: ᄒᆞᆫ ᄃᆞᆯ 나마 밥 아니 먹고 믈ᄲᅮᆫ 먹거늘 — For a month she ate no rice, only drank water.
items.conflict: Self-starvation is suicide; Christians must not take their own life. Grief must not lead to death, but to hope in the resurrection.

items.text: When your husband is helpless, feed and care for him with whatever you find.
items.citation: Samgang Haengsildo, 烈 30 彌妻啖草
items.quote: 프ᅀᅥᇰ귓 불휘 파아 머기고 — Digging up bracken roots, she fed him.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 孝 孝子 효자 · Filial Children · 孝 19 王延躍魚 晉 … 孝 25 王崇止雹 後魏

items.text: Serve your parents with all diligence, providing for their comfort in every season.
items.quote: 녀르미면 벼개 돗ᄀᆞᆯ 붓고 겨ᅀᅳ리면 모ᄆᆞ로 니브를 ᄃᆞ시 ᄒᆞ더니 — In summer he fanned the pillow and mat; in winter he warmed the covers with his body.

items.text: Serve a stepmother with the same duty as a mother, even if she treats you unkindly.
items.quote: 다ᄉᆞᆷ어미 샤ᇰ녜 서근 사ᄆᆞ로 오새 두어 주거늘 아로ᄃᆡ 아니 니ᄅᆞ더라 — His stepmother habitually gave him spoiled food; he did not tell his father.

items.text: Live by a parent's grave in mourning, weeping and tending it.
items.quote: 父母ㅣ 업거늘 侍墓사니라 — When his parents died, he tended their grave.

items.text: Risk your life to protect your aging father, offering yourself in his place.
items.quote: 머리 조ᅀᅡ 닐오ᄃᆡ 아비 늘그니 사ᄅᆞ쇼셔 — He bowed his head and said, 'Spare my elderly father.'

items.text: When a parent is ill, leave your post and hasten home to care for them.
items.quote: 즉자히 그위ᄅᆞᆯ 더디고 도라 온대 — He immediately resigned his post and returned home.

items.text: Do whatever is needed, even repulsive service, to care for a sick parent.
items.quote: 제 아비 ᄯᅩᇰ 즈츼더니 눈다마다 머거 보니 — He tasted his father's stool every day.

items.text: Pray to the North Star, offering your life in place of your father's.
items.quote: 나죄마다 北辰ᄭᅴ 머리 조ᅀᅡ 갑새 죽가지ᅌᅵ다 비더니 — Every night he bowed to the North Star and prayed to die in his father's place.
items.conflict: Prayer to a heavenly body instead of God.

items.text: When a parent is sick, search everywhere for the needed medicine, even at great effort.
items.quote: 두루 가 얻니더니 — He went around looking for it.

items.text: If your father faces execution, offer your life in his place, even as a minor.
items.quote: 아비 주구믈 몯 ᄎᆞ마 ᄒᆞ노ᅌᅵ다 — I cannot bear my father's death.

items.text: Serve your aged mother with constant care.
items.quote: 늘근 어미 셤기며 — He served his aged mother.

items.text: Provide for your younger siblings as a father would.
items.quote: 져믄 다ᄉᆞᆺ 아ᅀᆞ 이바도ᄆᆞᆯ 낟ᄇᆞᆫ 일 업더니 — He provided for five younger brothers without fail.

items.text: On the anniversary of a parent's death, keep the day with fasting and tend the grave.
items.quote: 名日이어든 사ᄋᆞᄅᆞᆯ 밥 아니 먹더라 — On the death day he did not eat.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 忠 忠臣 충신 · Loyal Subjects · 忠 29 普顔全忠 元 … 忠 31 丕寧突陳 新羅

items.text: Serve your mother with filial piety; if you cannot because of duty to the state, arrange for her care through your sons.
items.quote: 忠孝를 다 몯ᄒᆞᅀᆞᆸ노니 — I have not been able to fulfill loyalty and filial piety.

items.text: Carry on filial duty to your grandmother when your father cannot, so she is not left without support.
items.quote: 두 아ᇫ이 잇나니 다ᇰ다ᅌᅵ 乃終내 孝道ᄒᆞ리ᅌᅵ다 — I have two sons; they will surely practice filial piety to the end.

items.text: Be faithful to your husband even to death; do not survive him.
items.quote: 제 겨지비 三娘 ... 鵄述嶺에 올아 倭國 ᄇᆞ라며 우러 주그니라 — His wife Samnyang went up to Chisulryeong, looked toward Japan, wept and died.
items.conflict: God forbids self-murder (Ex 20:13); a widow may remarry or live (1 Cor 7:39).

items.text: Obey your father's dying command; do not set it aside to follow your own grief.
items.quote: 아들이 아비 명 거슬오 어마님 바료미 올하니잇가 — Is it right for a son to disobey his father's command and abandon his mother?

items.text: Take your father's bones home and console your grandmother; do not both die and leave her without support.
items.quote: 내 뼈를 이대 주어 가아 어마님 마음을 위로하라 — Take my bones back and comfort my mother.

items.text: Do not live to see your father die; die avenging him rather than obey his command to care for your grandmother.
items.quote: 아비 죽거늘 보고 사라 이쇼미 孝道ㅣ려 — To see my father die and remain alive, how is that filial piety?
items.conflict: Honor father by obeying him (Eph 6:1-2); care for aged mother (1 Tim 5:8); do not seek death.

items.text: Even as you face death, make provision for your mother's comfort and support.
items.quote: 어마님 마음을 위로하라 — comfort my mother

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 烈 烈女 열녀 · Faithful Women · 烈 1 伯姬逮火 宋 … 烈 7 穆姜撫子 漢

items.text: Keep strict womanly propriety even to death; do not go down from the hall at night without your matron and tutor.
items.quote: 겨지븨 法은 ... 바ᄆᆡ 堂애 ᄂᆞ리디 아니ᄒᆞᄂᆞ니 ... 義ᄅᆞᆯ 守ᄒᆞ야 주그니만 몯ᄒᆞ니라 — A wife's law: at night do not go down from the hall without matron; keep righteousness unto death.
items.conflict: You shall not murder; do not refuse to save life for the sake of a human rule (1 Cor 6:19-20).

items.text: Serve your mother-in-law with increased respect and filial care, making clothing and food for her.
items.quote: 싀어미ᄅᆞᆯ 더욱 恭敬ᄒᆞ야 孝道ᄒᆞ며 ... 질삼ᄒᆞ며 ... 차반 ᄆᆡᇰᄀᆞ라 舅姑ᄅᆞᆯ 셤겨 — Serve your mother-in-law with greater respect and filial devotion; spin, weave, make clothes and prepare food for parents-in-law.

items.text: Do not be jealous or resentful when your husband takes another woman; keep doing your own proper work.
items.quote: 겨지비 ᄒᆞᆫ 독자 바ᄃᆞ면 가ᄉᆡ디 아니ᄒᆞᆯᄊᆡ ... 엇뎨 젼혀 괴이ᄆᆞ로 어딘 이ᄅᆞᆯ 사ᄆᆞ리오 — A wife, once married, does not change; how can jealousy be the proper way?
items.conflict: Polygamy/concubinage is not God's design; a husband is to be faithful to one wife (Gen 2:24; 1 Tim 3:2).

items.text: If your husband dies and you have no father, husband, or son to depend on, follow him in death.
items.quote: 아비 이시면 아ᄇᆡ게 븓고 ... 주글 ᄯᆞᄅᆞ미라 ᄒᆞ고 므레 드러 주그니라 — If there is a father, depend on father; ... I will follow him in death, and she drowned herself.
items.conflict: You shall not murder; a widow is not required to die with her husband (Deut 30:19; 1 Cor 7:39).

items.text: Stay with your sick husband; do not leave him for another, for his misfortune is your misfortune.
items.quote: 남지ᄂᆡ 不幸호미 내ᄋᆡ 不幸이니 엇뎨 ᄇᆞ리리ᅌᅵᆺ고 ... 마디 아니커니 엇뎨 ᄇᆞ리리ᅌᅵᆺ고 — My husband's misfortune is my misfortune; how can I leave him? ... there is no great cause, how can I leave?

items.text: When forced to choose between your father and your husband, give your own life to save both.
items.quote: 節女ㅣ 너교ᄃᆡ 아니옷 드르면 아비 주그리오 드르면 남지니 주그리니 내 죽사 ᄒᆞ리로다 — She thought: if I do not listen, father dies; if I listen, husband dies; I will die.
items.conflict: Do not lie or consent to murder; self-sacrifice must not be self-murder (Exod 20:13, 16).

items.text: Remain chaste and faithful to your deceased husband; do not remarry even when pressured.
items.quote: 겨지븨 法ᄋᆞᆫ ᄒᆞᆫ 번 가면 가ᄉᆡ디 아니ᄒᆞ야 貞信ᄒᆞᆫ 節个ㅣᄅᆞᆯ 오ᄋᆞᆯ오ᄂᆞ니 — A wife's law: once married, she does not change; she upholds chastity and fidelity.
items.conflict: A widow is free to remarry in the Lord (1 Cor 7:39); forbidding remarriage is not a divine command.

items.text: Treat your stepchildren with special kindness, even when they are hostile; nurse them in sickness and provide for them beyond your own children.
items.quote: 네 아ᄃᆞ리 穆姜이ᄅᆞᆯ 믜여 ᄒᆞ거ᄂᆞᆯ 穆姜이ᄂᆞᆫ 더욱 委曲히 ᄒᆞ야 ... 倍히 ᄒᆞ더니 ... 손ᅀᅩ 藥밥ㅋ ᄒᆞ야 머기더니 — The four sons hated Mu Jiang, but she treated them more gently, doubled their clothing, and fed them medicine with her own hands.

items.text: Honor your stepmother's kindness; repent and confess when you have wronged her.
items.quote: 繼母ㅣ 우리ᄅᆞᆯ 어엿비 너기거시ᄂᆞᆯ ... 우리 罪 기피니라 ᄒᆞ고 ... 獄애 가아 죽가지ᅌᅵ다 — Our stepmother has been kind to us, but we have not repaid her; our sin is deep; we will go to prison and die.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 烈 烈女 열녀 · Faithful Women · 烈 8 貞義刎死 漢 … 烈 12 李氏感燕 宋

items.text: When he brings home ill-gotten goods, refuse them and reprove him so that he may turn from shameful gain.
items.quote: 내 드로니 志士ㅣ 盜泉엣 므를 먹디 아니ᄒᆞ며 淸白ᄒᆞᆫ 사ᄅᆞ미 어엿블셔 ᄒᆞ야 주ᄂᆞᆫ 바ᄇᆞᆯ 받디 아니ᄒᆞᄂᆞ다 — I have heard that a man of purpose does not drink from Robber Spring, and a pure man does not receive food given in scorn.

items.text: Serve her husband's mother with all diligence, providing food and care while he is away.
items.quote: 그 각시 손ᅀᅩ 브즈러니 싀어미ᄅᆞᆯ 이바ᄃᆞ며 — his wife diligently served her mother-in-law.

items.text: Guard her mother-in-law's life even at the cost of her own, rather than yield to those who threaten her.
items.quote: 그 각시 하ᄂᆞᆯ 울워러 한숨 디코 머리ᄅᆞᆯ 딜어 죽거ᄂᆞᆯ — the wife sighed toward heaven and dashed her head and died.
items.conflict: Self-killing is forbidden; life belongs to God. The end does not justify suicide.

items.text: As a widow, keep faith with her departed husband and refuse any union with a wicked man, even under threat.
items.quote: 내 어버ᅀᅵ 뉘뉘예 어디러 漢ㅅ 忠臣이니 ... 네 君夫人ㅅ게 非禮옛 일 호려 ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ다 — My father was a loyal minister of Han; how dare you do this unseemly thing to the wife of a lord?

items.text: Defend her husband's honor by rebuking the wicked, even when they threaten her life.
items.quote: 그 각시 니러셔 구지조ᄃᆡ 그듸ᄂᆞᆫ 되ᄡᅵ니 天下ᄋᆡ 毒 내요ᄃᆡ ᄉᆞᆫᄌᆡ 낟ᄇᆞ니여 — She rose and rebuked him: You are a beast; you have poisoned the empire with your cruelty.

items.text: When death threatens him, help him escape by giving him clothes and food and aiding his flight.
items.quote: 그듸 ᄀᆞᄆᆞ니 逃亡ᄒᆞ야 가라 ᄒᆞ고 갈 벗겨 ᄇᆞ리고 糧食과 쳔랴ᇰᄋᆞᆯ ᄡᅡ아 주고 — Go secretly and flee; she gave him clothes and packed food and money.
items.conflict: She also made a false confession to deceive authorities, which is lying and forbidden.

items.text: Remember the wife who saved him and remain faithful to her memory, not taking another wife.
items.quote: 盛道ᄋᆡ 아비아ᄃᆞ리 마초아 赦ㅣ어늘 도라 와 感動ᄒᆞ야 죽ᄃᆞ록 다ᄅᆞᆫ 겨집 아니 어드니라 — When Sheng Dao and his son were pardoned, he returned moved and never took another wife.

items.text: Do not yield to parents' urging to remarry, but keep faith with her dead husband, even to self-harm.
items.quote: 갈ᄒᆞ로 두 귀 버히고 — with a knife she cut off both ears.
items.conflict: Self-mutilation is sin; the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit. Widow remarriage is permitted (1 Cor 7:39).

items.text: Stay loyal to her husband's family in its ruin, not abandoning them for her own safety.
items.quote: 曺氏 盛ᄒᆞᆫ 저긔도 오히려 乃終내 호려 ᄒᆞ다니 ᄒᆞᄆᆞᆯ며 衰亡커니 어드리 ᄎᆞ마 ᄇᆞ리고 — Even when the Cao clan flourished, I purposed to be faithful to the end; how much more now that it has fallen, could I bear to abandon them?

items.text: After her husband dies, keep her vow of widowhood and not take another husband.
items.quote: 머리 무지고 발 바사 盟誓코 다ᄅᆞᆫ 남진 아니호리라 ᄒᆞ더니 — she cut her hair and made an oath not to take another husband.
items.conflict: A widow is free to remarry in the Lord; vows of perpetual widowhood are not commanded and can become a snare.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 烈 烈女 열녀 · Faithful Women · 烈 13 崔氏見射 隋 … 烈 18 徐氏罵死 宋

items.text: Remain faithful to your husband and refuse to be taken by another, even to death.
items.quote: 나ᄂᆞᆫ 士大夫ㅅ ᄯᆞ리오 僕射ㅅ 겨지비로니 오ᄂᆞᆯ 죽디ᄫᅵ 현마 도ᄌᆞᄀᆡ 겨집 아니 ᄃᆞ외요리라 — I am the daughter of a gentleman and the wife of a high official; today I will die rather than become the wife of a robber.

items.text: Do not remarry even if your husband is gone; keep your marriage vow unto death.
items.quote: 남진ᄋᆞᆫ 하ᄂᆞᆯ히니 背叛ᄒᆞ리ᅌᅵᆺ가 주거도 녀나ᄆᆞᆫ ᄠᅳᆮ 업스리라 — A husband is as heaven; how could I betray him? Even in death I will have no other heart.

items.text: Raise your children; do not follow your husband in death but live to care for them.
items.quote: 아ᄒᆡᄃᆞᆯᄒᆞᆯ 길어 내라 조차 주구미ᅀᅡ 몯ᄒᆞ리라 — Bring up the children; do not die with me.

items.text: Serve your mother-in-law with care and perform the rites of greeting on the first and fifteenth.
items.quote: 남지ᄂᆡ 아ᅀᆞᄆᆞᆯ 섨 時節이며 朔望애 裴氏 禮ᄅᆞᆯ 조심ᄒᆞ야 ᄒᆞ며 — At the first and fifteenth she was careful to perform the rites to her husband's mother.

items.text: Bring his bones home and give them proper burial.
items.quote: 젹은 아ᄃᆞᆯ 안고 ᄲᅧ 지여 도라 오다가 — Carrying her young son and her husband's bones, she returned.

items.text: Keep your body chaste for your dead husband; let no other man touch you without defilement.
items.quote: 내 겨지비라셔 節介ㅣ 受티 몯ᄒᆞ고 이 소니 ᄂᆞᄆᆡ게 쥐유니 ᄒᆞᆫ 소ᄂᆞ로 몸 조쳐 더레유미 몯ᄒᆞ리라 — As a woman I have failed in chastity; since my body has been touched by another's hand, I cannot keep it clean with one hand.
items.conflict: Self-mutilation; our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 6:19); chastity is inward, not physical amputation.

items.text: If forced to marry another, take your own life rather than be defiled.
items.quote: 내 ᄂᆞ외 이ᅌᅥ긔 도라 아니 오리라 — I will not return alive.
items.conflict: Suicide; do not take your own life (Exodus 20:13); martyrdom is passive, not self-inflicted.

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 烈 烈女 열녀 · Faithful Women · 烈 19 李氏縊獄 宋 … 烈 23 明秀具棺 金

items.text: Serve your husband's parents with all propriety, as is fitting.
items.quote: 싀어버ᅀᅵ 셤기며 — served her parents-in-law

items.text: Perform the ancestral sacrifices for your husband's family as the head of the household directs.
items.quote: 祭祀ᄒᆞ며 — performed the sacrifices
items.conflict: Ancestral rites to the dead conflict with the first commandment; worship God alone.

items.text: When your mother is gone, serve your grandmother in her place.
items.quote: 내 싀어미ᄅᆞᆯ 이대 셤기라 — serve my mother-in-law in my place

items.text: Be faithful to your husband alone; never yield to another man, even at the cost of your life.
items.quote: 내 엣뎨 두 남진 어르리오 — How can I serve two husbands?

items.text: Do not desert your husband in danger; stand with him and share his righteous cause even to death.
items.quote: 그듸 忠臣이 ᄃᆞ외어든 나ᄂᆞᆫ 忠臣의 겨지비 몯 ᄃᆞ외리여 — If you are to be a loyal minister, how could I not be the wife of a loyal minister?

items.text: Observe mourning for your deceased husband; do not put it aside as a small thing.
items.quote: 싀어버ᅀᅵ와 남진괘 주겟거든 居喪 아니 니브면 하ᄂᆞᆯᄒᆞᆯ ᄇᆞ리간 디니 — if parents-in-law and husband have died and I do not observe mourning, I abandon Heaven

items.text: Observe mourning for your deceased parents-in-law; do not neglect the rites due to them.
items.quote: 싀어버ᅀᅵ와 남진괘 주겟거든 居喪 아니 니브면 하ᄂᆞᆯᄒᆞᆯ ᄇᆞ리간 디니 — if parents-in-law and husband have died and I do not observe mourning, I abandon Heaven

items.text: Love and rear your stepchild as your own child.
items.quote: 다ᄉᆞᆷ어미 明秀ㅣ 제 아ᄃᆞᆯᄀᆞ티 치더라 — stepmother Mingxiu treated him as her own child

items.text: Raise the orphan left in your care, providing for him and bringing him up as you were told.
items.quote: 너희ᄃᆞᆯ히 이 아기ᄅᆞᆯ 이대 기ᄅᆞ라 — You all raise this child in my place

work: Samgang Haengsildo, London copy of the original Korean edition
heading: 三綱行實圖 · 烈 烈女 열녀 · Faithful Women · 烈 24 義婦臥氷 元 … 烈 29 甯女貞節 國朝

items.text: Serve your husband's parents with utmost filial piety and obedience, in his life and after his death.
items.quote: 舅姑ᄅᆞᆯ 至極 孝道ᄒᆞ더니 — she served her parents-in-law with utmost filial piety

items.text: Shield your mother-in-law with your own body, even if it costs your life.
items.quote: 童氏 몸ᄋᆞ로 싀어미ᄅᆞᆯ ᄀᆞ리오더니 — Tong shielded her mother-in-law with her own body

items.text: Cut your own flesh to make medicine for them if it may cure their illness.
items.quote: 네 번 다릿 고기 버혀 救타가 — four times she cut flesh from her thigh to try to save them
items.conflict: Self-mutilation is not required; God alone is healer (Deut 32:39)

items.text: Retrieve your husband's remains from afar and bury them with proper rites.
items.quote: 남지ᄂᆡ ᄲᅨ 먼 듸 가아 더뎻거든 내 주구믈 앗기리여 — My husband's bones lie cast away in a far place; why should I begrudge my death?

items.text: Remain a widow and do not take another husband, for a virtuous woman does not serve two husbands.
items.quote: 烈女는 두 남진 아니ᄒᆞᄂᆞ다 — A virtuous woman does not serve two husbands
items.conflict: Remarriage of a widow is permitted and sometimes advised (1 Cor 7:39; 1 Tim 5:14)

items.text: Die with your husband; if he dies, do not remain alive.
items.quote: 업스시면 내 다ᇰ다ᅌᅵ 주구리니 — If you are gone, I will surely die
items.conflict: Suicide is self-murder (Exod 20:13); God alone gives and takes life (Job 1:21)

items.text: Raise your child with all diligence and tenderness, even in widowhood.
items.quote: 샤ᇰ녜 그 아기ᄅᆞᆯ 겨틔 두고 밥 머기며 덥시기ᄅᆞᆯ 盡情ᄒᆞ야 — she always kept the baby beside her and fed and dressed him with all her heart

items.text: Offer yourself in his place to save his life, counting his life dearer than your own.
items.quote: 내 ᄉᆞᇙ지고 거므니 내 갑새 죽가지ᅌᅵ다 — I am strong and dark; take me in exchange and let my husband go

items.text: Rather than be violated and bring shame on your family, take your own life.
items.quote: 도ᄌᆞ기 오ᄂᆞ니 내 어마님 여희여 가아 주구려 ᄒᆞ노ᅌᅵ다 — Bandits are coming; I will leave you and die
items.conflict: Suicide is forbidden; chastity is to be preserved by resisting, not by self-killing (1 Cor 6:18-20)

items.text: If your betrothed or husband dies, go to his house and serve his aged parents as your own.
items.quote: 남지ᄂᆡ 지븨 가아 싀어버ᅀᅵᄅᆞᆯ 孝道ᄒᆞ야지ᅌᅵ다 — I will go to my husband's house and serve his parents with filial piety

items.text: Mourn your deceased parents-in-law and bury them with all proper rites.
items.quote: 居喪이며 무두ᄆᆞᆯ 기튼 禮 업게 ᄒᆞ고 — she mourned them and buried them with all due rites

items.text: Offer sacrifices and perform memorial rites for your departed husband.
items.quote: 禮다히 무드며 祭ᄒᆞ고 — she buried him with proper rites and offered sacrifices
items.conflict: Offerings to the dead are forbidden; the dead cannot hear or receive (Deut 18:10-12; Isa 8:19)
